view-01.png.evidence: Cutaway rooms have convincing wall depth, warm/cool illumination, wooden and tiled floors, furniture and restrained tactical marks.

view-02.png.evidence: Fog, autumn vegetation, muddy ruts and weathered buildings create rich physical depth; gray tanks blend with terrain at this scale.

view-03.png.evidence: Small service structures and a dirt compound give the airfield purpose; lighter player edging separates it from roofs, but ground remains broad mottling and roofs are simple planes.

view-04.png.evidence: Produce stalls, wood, stone and fabric show distinct material and shadow treatment; tactical paths remain visible among dense figures.

view-05.png.evidence: Full-width tan carrier deck contrasts with water and long wake is visible; cream aircraft overlap the similarly pale deck, limiting local silhouette clarity.

view-06.png.evidence: Sharp fenced service compound, small sheds, tracks, hangars and runway form a coherent airfield; shaded trees add depth, although grass and road material remain simplified.

view-07.png.evidence: Blue-white player edge improves separation from mottled grass; muted varied tree crowns and a partial service compound enrich the coast, but all surfaces remain soft.

view-08.png.evidence: Mottled olive ground, shore rocks and dark hangar sides provide variety; runway reads clearly but grass still looks like blurred broad texture.

view-09.png.evidence: Sharp deck strips and clearer outer carrier shape sit against teal water with a long wake; pale aircraft still merge with pale deck at overlap points.

view-10.png.evidence: Narrow striped deck and dark hull add structure with a coherent wake, but the dark outer band weakens ship-water separation.

view-11.png.evidence: Plank-like deck strips, hull band, bow foam and long wake enrich the quiet ship; metallic response and hull-water contact remain modest.

view-12.png.evidence: Detailed narrow deck, bow foam and long wake remain visible beneath a crowd; many identical cream wings and soft particles obscure the player.

view-13.png.evidence: Mottled olive grass and faint field rows enrich coastline with grounded trees and stones; material definition stays soft.

view-14.png.evidence: Sharp deck striping, dark hull edge and long wake give form; outer hull blends with water and aircraft crowd the near end.

view-15.png.evidence: Layered explosion rays, sparks and bloom integrate with detailed machinery and atmospheric cliffs; the bright blast obscures nearby silhouettes.

view-16.png.evidence: Broad pale deck makes quiet carrier silhouette clear against water; striped deck, raised bridge and wake add form, while surface lighting remains simple.

view-17.png.evidence: Uncrowded full-width tan deck separates cleanly from teal water; bridge and long wake help volume, but soft strips and flat shading limit material depth.

view-18.png.evidence: Deck strips and long wake add interest beneath clear aircraft; soft edges and dark outer hull reduce separation from water.

view-19.png.evidence: Sharp hangars and runway sit on varied olive grass with rocks and sand transition; richer texture still lacks small-scale physical light response.

view-20.png.evidence: Busy ship has varied deck strips and bow foam; lighter shadows help relative to dark duplicate shapes, but crowded planes and dots still hide the player.

view-21.png.evidence: Player edging, more natural tree tones and partial service-compound detail strengthen hierarchy; coast remains sparse and fields are still rectangular patches.

view-22.png.evidence: Broad tan deck is visible beneath a dense cream-aircraft swarm; wake and dots convey activity, but wing/deck colors are similar and player remains hard to isolate.

view-23.png.evidence: Sharper broad deck and long wake make the ship coherent; overlapping pale planes and particle dots remain the dominant readability problem.

view-24.png.evidence: Wet reflections, rain, smoke and bright tracer light integrate convincingly; small dark infantry remain hard to read at phone size.

view-25.png.evidence: Sharper trees, stones, hangars and field rows complement olive ground; water flecks add activity but appear partly detached from underlying waves.

visible_regressions.comparison: The full pale deck improves overall ship-water separation versus dark-border versions, but cream wings overlap a more similarly colored surface. This is a local contrast tradeoff; swarm player readability remains low.

top3_gaps: Material depth is still modest: deck, hangar roofs, grass and sand lack physically varied surface illumination despite added detail.
The player remains difficult to isolate within the crowded carrier views; brighter edging helps coastal views much more than overlapping aircraft.
Ship wakes are coherent but schematic pale streaks; surrounding white flecks and soft spark dots are only loosely integrated.
recommendations: Prioritize a player-only edge/contrast cue that remains distinct over both tan deck and cream aircraft, with nearby particles subdued.
Keep new service compounds; add restrained ground contact and surface-specific shading to roofs, aprons, dirt tracks and carrier deck rather than more global texture noise.
Give ship wake a hull-connected foam base, gradual width/opacity variation and coherent small streak direction; maintain strong outer hull-water contrast.
_summary.blinding_limitations: Viewed all 25 PNGs and did not open mapping, source or outside files. Familiar reference/control compositions are recognizable and exact established score vectors were retained when visually unchanged. Comparative remarks refer to appearances, not assumed chronology.
